texts: mixed: the rule fires and reads correctly, but two links go missing — nothing records that Sunken Cove is a cove, and the tending never reaches the individual Keepers, so a later question about one named Keeper finds nothing. The second is worth a one-word edit that spells out the per-Keeper reading: 'When the feather store at the Watch is large, each Keeper tends the Sunken Cove lanterns safely in winter.' The missing cove type is parser variance — your next sentence with the same phrase got it — so no rewording of this one addresses it.

bad: the conditional collapses — the parse asserts flat out both that the Watch's feather store IS large and that the Keepers DO tend the lanterns safely, so your 'when' restriction is dropped and every Keeper's safe tending is claimed unconditionally. A bare 'when' whose participants are all definite ('the Watch's feather store', 'the Keepers', 'the Sunken Cove lanterns') reads as a one-off narrative rather than a standing rule, so use the explicit recurrence word and make the distribution explicit: 'Whenever the Watch's feather store is large, each Keeper tends the Sunken Cove lanterns safely.'
good. the Sunken-Cove premodifier, the winter slot and the habitual present all land, with the Council kept as one collective actor and the rations recorded as what is issued.
good. a fireable rule tying the growth of wraith risk to each occasion of the store being small, with both compounds linked to their head nouns.
